result.topic_en: Euler gives the correction that takes the shadow's longitude to the Moon's true longitude in its orbit at mid-eclipse, and tabulates it against the Moon's distance from its ascending node.
result.transcription:
De loco lunae ex eclipsibus lunaribus determinando. 369

aequalitatem concluditur
longitudo lunae $L = U - \frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x \,\mathrm{tang}^2 \frac{1}{2}\varrho}{g(n-m)}$ sec.
§ 12. Hoc igitur jam sumus consecuti, ut pro eclipsis momento medio veram lunae longitudinem in orbita assignare valeamus. Pro isto scilicet momento quaeri debet longitudo solis vera, quae sex signis vel aucta vel minuta dabit longitudinem umbrae $U$: ab hac porro subtrahantur $\frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho}{g(n-m)}$ minuta secunda*), atque remanebit longitudo lunae in orbita tempore medio eclipsis. Ad hoc ergo nosse oportet arcum $x$, qui habetur si longitudo nodi ascendentis a longitudine centri umbrae in media eclipsi subtrahatur: quamquam autem ob theoriam nondum satis perfectam, longitudo nodi nondum exactissime est cognita; tamen hinc ista determinatio non turbatur, quoniam sufficit locum nodi proxime saltem nosse, dum error aliquot minutorum in arcu $x$ commissus nullum sensibilem errorem in valore $\frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho}{g(n-m)}$ gignit.
§ 13. Simili modo ex tabulis lunaribus adhuc constructis satis exacte habetur angulus inclinationis $☊ = \varrho$, ut minimus error in eo commissus nihili sit aestimandus. Quamobrem pro quovis angulo $x$ valor $\frac{1}{g}\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho$ satis exacte assignari et in minutis secundis exprimi poterit, quem deinceps per $\frac{m+n+2k}{n-m} = 1 + \frac{2(m+k)}{n-m}$ multiplicari oportet, ut particula a longitudine umbrae subtrahenda obtineatur. Neglecto autem isto multiplicatore $\frac{m+n+2k}{n-m}$, valor alterius $\frac{1}{g}\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho$ ita se habebit, ut sequens tabella exhibet:

Tabula aequationum
pro vera lunae longitudine in orbita, tempore medio eclipsis lunaris invenienda.
Subtrahatur longitudo nodi a longitudine umbrae, et aequatio, quam sequens tabella exhibet, applicetur ad locum soli oppositum.

Scripturae in margine. Hae autem aequationes insuper multiplicari debent per factorem $1+\frac{2(m+k)}{n-m}$ ex motu horario inveniendum.
Multiplicatae per $2\frac{1}{6}$ dant correctionem pro longitudine lunae in ecliptica; multiplicatae autem per $\frac{2n+2k}{n-m}$ dabunt correctionem pro longitudine vera in ecliptica.
$n = 2023'' - 258''\cos v$, $m = 148''$, $k = 8$
si $\cos v = 0$, $\frac{4062}{1875}$, si $\cos v = 1$, $\frac{3546}{1875}$,
si $\cos v = -1$, $\frac{4578}{1875}$.

*) Scriptura ad marg.: et si a loco lunae in orbita subtrahatur part. $\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho$ habebitur longitudo vera in ecliptica.

L. Euleri Op. posthuma T. II. 47

items.quote: tamen hinc ista determinatio non turbatur, quoniam sufficit locum nodi proxime saltem nosse, dum error aliquot minutorum in arcu $x$ commissus nullum sensibilem errorem in valore $\frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\varrho}{g(n-m)}$ gignit.
items.english: Yet this determination is not disturbed, since it suffices to know the node's position at least approximately, because an error of a few minutes in the arc x produces no sensible error in the value of the correction.

items.quote: satis exacte habetur angulus inclinationis $☊ = \varrho$, ut minimus error in eo commissus nihili sit aestimandus.
items.english: The angle of inclination ρ is known exactly enough from existing lunar tables that the very small error in it may be counted as nothing.
